giulio.benedetti@utu.fi

methods.Rmd

Introduction

Definitions

The table below summarises the technical terms used to make sense of ariadne in its vignettes and underlying code.

Term Definition Examples
Feature type A distinct type of biological entity with unique elements labeled by IDs. Written in lowercase for consistency. genes (KEGG genes ID), ko (KEGG Orthologues), ec (Enzyme Commission number), uniref90 (UniRef sequence clusters)
Level A unique element belonging to a feature type. Often referred to as a feature. 563 (NCBI ID for E. coli), C00246 (KEGG compound ID for butyrate), P0DTC2 (UniProtKB ID for SARS-CoV-2 spike protein)
Linkmap A 2-column data frame with feature types as columns and their links in the rows. Named as x2y, where x and y are feature types. tax2cpd (linkmap between taxon names and compounds)
Resource A database from which linkmaps between feature types can be retrieved. KEGG, Rhea, UniProt
Weave The operation of sequentially linking feature types to create a new linkmap between two previously unlinked feature types. Uses the syntax x ~ y, where x is the origin and y is the target feature type. ko ~ ec, disease ~ drug, genes ~ metacyc

Technical details: strengths and limitations

The ariadne approach provides several advantages to streamline the mapping workflow. However, it also presents certain downsides worth considering.

Graph-based resource representation

Graph-based resource representation | Focused on established databases

Graph-based resource representation using an igraph object where edges are resources and nodes are feature types, enabling graph theory for path selection and easy expansion with custom resources.

Focused on established databases. Less permanent ones may be added manually by the user. This is to reduce the odds of unpredicted changes or disappearing of underlying resources.

Not always possible to track new databases reproducibly. Many databases do not provide programmatic access (or even links) to their resources, and do not keep past releases accessible, so we do not include them in the core graph, even though can be manually added by users.

Resource query optimisation

Fast queries | Internet access required

Fast queries: with httr2 for API requests and SPARQL for even faster linkmap retrieval when possible.

Resource storage and caching

Efficient caching and storage | Not supported for all resources

Efficient caching and storage: to automatically cache linkmaps with BiocFileCache and store them in the efficient Apache Parquet format via arrow.

Cross-resource linkmap generation

Optimised linkmap generation | Code complexity increases with resource coverage

Optimised linkmap generation through the multifactor class, which streamlines factor operations to create linkmaps by sequentially combining them along the path from origin to target feature type.
